subtopics.title: The State in the Market — Taxes, Subsidies and Price Controls

questions.question: A tax on a product shifts:
options: The SUPPLY curve LEFT and up by the tax — higher price, smaller quantity, burden shared between buyer and seller
The supply curve right and down

questions.question: A maximum price only affects the market when it is set:
options: BELOW equilibrium — where it opens a permanent shortage with queues, rationing and black markets

questions.question: A minimum price set above equilibrium causes:
options: A permanent SURPLUS the state must buy up, store or export at a cost to the budget

questions.question: The honest two-sided evaluation of the minimum wage is:
options: It has no effect on the labour market
It raises the incomes of workers who keep employment, while at a wage above equilibrium the quantity of labour demanded can fall

subtopics.title: From Barter to Industry — the Evolution of Markets

questions.question: The DOUBLE COINCIDENCE OF WANTS is the requirement that:
options: Each trader must find someone who HAS what they want AND WANTS what they have — barter's built-in brake
Two goods must have equal value

questions.question: Money's four functions are:
options: Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, and standard of deferred payment

questions.question: Governments entered growing markets to:
options: Issue and protect currency, enforce contracts, regulate quality, tax trade, and provide what markets will not

questions.question: South Africa's industrial development was driven inland by:
options: The MINERAL REVOLUTION — diamonds and gold pulling railways, capital and labour to the interior

subtopics.title: Population, Labour and the Rules of Work

questions.question: The labour force consists of:
options: Everyone aged 15 to 64 who is employed PLUS everyone unemployed but actively seeking work

questions.question: The demand for labour is DERIVED demand because:
options: Hiring follows the demand for what workers PRODUCE — nobody hires for its own sake

questions.question: The Act that sets maximum ordinary hours, leave and notice beneath every contract is:
options: The BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT — the floor under every job

questions.question: The dispute ladder at the CCMA runs:
options: CONCILIATION where a commissioner helps parties settle, then ARBITRATION where the commissioner decides, with matters of law going to the Labour Court

questions.question: The unemployment rate divides the unemployed by:
options: The LABOUR FORCE — never by the population

questions.question: South Africa's DOMINANT type of unemployment is:
options: STRUCTURAL — skills or locations mismatched to what employers need, cured by education, training and spatial remedies

questions.question: Redress through the four factors of production pairs:
options: Land with restitution, redistribution and tenure; labour with equity and skills; capital with ownership, procurement and finance; entrepreneurship with small-business support

questions.question: NEDLAC seats which four constituencies before major economic laws reach Parliament?
"Ceilings make queues" because pinning a price below the market level means:
options: Sellers offer LESS while buyers want MORE — and the gap becomes queues, rationing and back-door sales
Sellers offer more than buyers want

questions.question: Brown bread and maize meal carrying no VAT while most goods carry fifteen percent is an example of:
options: The state making essentials CHEAPER on purpose so more families afford them

questions.question: "Floors make piles" means a price pinned ABOVE the market level produces:
options: A SURPLUS somebody must buy, store or ship out

subtopics.title: From Swapping Goats to Swiping Cards

questions.question: The "wasted morning at the river" happens because:
options: The fisherman wants a goat, not maize — the double coincidence of wants fails and the swap collapses

questions.question: As the "go-between", money:
options: Ends the double coincidence — the fisherman takes coins and buys his goat elsewhere

questions.question: Money as the "promise-keeper" refers to its function as:
options: A STANDARD OF DEFERRED PAYMENT — buy now, pay later becomes possible

questions.question: In the village story, the correct order of arrivals is:
options: Surplus and barter, then money, then the chief guarding coins and promises, then the machines and factories

subtopics.title: The Gate, the Team and the Starting Line

questions.question: The learner in class and the grandmother at rest are:
options: OFF the team — outside the labour force, not unemployed, just not playing

questions.question: "The employer's need is second-hand" means:
options: Hiring happens because customers are buying what those hands will make — derived demand

questions.question: "A field without seed money is not yet a farm" argues that redress instruments:
options: Need their PARTNERS — a title deed, learnership or tender falls short unless finance, jobs and support arrive together

questions.question: The five people in the queue at the gate represent:
options: Five reasons to leave the labour force
The five TYPES of unemployment — frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological — each needing its own fix
